summary: Business Line maintains an accumulate rating on PSU thermal power major NTPC, which has gained about 48% since its August 13, 2023 call. The stock is re-rated on earnings growth, an assured-return cost-plus PPA model, assured coal supply and aggressive renewable and thermal capacity addition plans. The note covers H1FY24 performance, growth plans, capex guidance and the planned NTPC Green Energy IPO.
one_line: Business Line keeps an accumulate rating on NTPC, citing assured-return PPAs, coal security, capacity expansion plans and a roughly 3% dividend yield.
key_facts: The Power Ministry has scheduled tenders of around 50 GW annually of renewable energy for the next five years, to reach a target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity.
NTPC stock has gained around 48 per cent since the accumulate rating dated August 13, 2023, with trailing P/E rising from about 10 times to 12 times.
NTPC trades at a one-year forward P/E of around 11 times, about 35 per cent above its five-year average P/E of around 8.2 times.
More than 90 per cent of NTPC's revenue is tied to long-term PPAs under a cost-plus tariff regime that allows ROE of 15.5 per cent.
NTPC has 20-year fuel supply agreements with Coal India Limited and Singareni Collieries Company Limited for an Annual Contracted Quantity of 183 MTPA, plus captive coal mining capacity of 71 MMT.
In H1FY24 NTPC's coal plant PAF was 93.32 per cent versus 92.05 per cent in H1FY23, and PLF was 76.62 per cent against a national average of 68.75 per cent.
H1FY24 generation rose around 4 per cent YoY to 212 billion units; revenue was flattish at close to ₹88,058.44 crore.
H1FY24 EBITDA grew around 18 per cent to ₹25,091 crore, with margins expanding from 25 per cent to 29 per cent due to a lower share of imported coal.
NTPC plans 130 GW of installed capacity including 60 GW of renewable energy from the current 3.3 GW, and aims to add 15-16 GW of renewables by FY26.
NTPC has raised its FY26 thermal capacity addition target to 10-11 GW from 7 GW earlier, implying 10-11 per cent capacity CAGR over FY23-26.
Capex guidance for FY24 is around ₹28,373 crore, with FY25 and FY26 on similar lines.
NTPC now plans an IPO of NTPC Green Energy Ltd rather than selling a stake to a strategic investor, with timing uncertain.
NTPC's D/E is around 1.24 times as of H1FY24, and its dividend yield is around 3 per cent.
